high_severity_items.summary: Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate 25bp to 5.50%, its first hike since 2023, citing ten straight months of rising retail inflation (4.8% in August) above its 4% target and shifting to a 'calibrated tightening' stance. The move aligns with broad global monetary tightening (Fed, BoJ, ECB, BOK) amid elevated energy and commodity prices, with the RBI flagging geopolitical tensions, trade frictions and tighter financial conditions as growth risks. India's growth remains resilient (FY27 estimate raised to 7.1%) but the World Bank sees moderation from 7.8%, while heavy fuel import dependence and Strait of Hormuz exposure plus El Nino-related food price risk add supply-side inflation pressure.
high_severity_items.title: India’s central bank hikes rates for the first time since 2023 as inflation risks build

high_severity_items.summary: IMF Managing Director Georgieva warns that AI's investment boom is simultaneously lifting global growth and stoking inflation, while a Gulf-war energy supply shock, oil above $100, record public debt and surging long-term bond yields squeeze fiscal space and raise financial-stability risk from hyperscaler leverage and concentrated U.S. equity holdings; she hints at a prudently hawkish monetary posture.
high_severity_items.title: Why AI is both the hope and the hazard for world leaders, according to IMF chief Georgieva
